title: The Judgment of the Wicked and the Cup of Wrath
english: The relatives of the archers should not say 'Repent like a sparrow' in a mocking way, which we shall reject, wanting to show those who trust in God with a whole heart.

Since the archers prepared to sophistize are sons of darkness and of night, those having a straight heart set themselves to shoot in the clear night. [Ps 10:3b] The Lord is righteous; what will he do? Will he lay snares upon the sinners and divide to them a cup of punishment, so that while drinking them they become weak from the impulse to shoot? [Ps 10:4-7] Concerning the Father, and also Him, the Savior: before the incarnation, His holy temple was to be rejected, having the holy and heavenly thought concerning Him. [Ps 10:4] In His holy temple and He has the throne in heaven, reigning divinely and supernaturally. We also noted that previously the throne was taken instead of the kingdom.

But the watchful ones and the powers of God, called His eyes, become toward the sufferer, guarding him harmless from those appointed around him. The eyelids of the eyes of God examine the actions and the thoughts of men. From this, the philanthropy of the Judge is shown. For if He examined with eyes and not with eyelids, the judgment would be unendurable to men. But His examining with His own eyelids does not mean all the sins of those judged are observed, nor do these exist in magnitude.

It is also possible to say: His eyes are upon the one being benefited, if a sufferer exists, but the eyelids are upon the sons; many men's sons, if the benefits are abundantly and boldly accomplished, but the punishments hide much concerning God. And these things he will say by thought; they show no perceptible eyelid or anything of that kind, therefore these things must be thought of in a God-befitting way. Christ is not to be revealed on a step; all must be brought to each one what he has done through the body, whether good or evil. Having said this, under the Lord's examination being done of the righteous and the ungodly, he brings it as if he hates his own soul, the one doing evil without hating it as injustice, making it subject to punishment because of sinning; he acts contrary to the one acting justly.

He who loves his soul and his neighbor as himself strives toward virtue. The Lord does not fight, but examines the righteous and the impious by the fact that the impious do not stand up in judgment. For the former signifies those who are entirely atheistic, while the latter signifies those who despise God because of sinning. For the Scriptures declare this, especially that which says, 'The righteous shall be like the impious' in Genesis.

He will lay snares upon sinners, that is, he will punish them by making snares and by keeping those being hunted within them, unless they are delivered up by him to the desires of their own hearts; this is also declared by the sufferings of dishonor and an unproven mind. And therefore, if not for this, it is said 'He will lay snares' rather than 'He will rain snares'; for those having been ensnared by themselves are being rained upon with snares. This is also declared from 'The Lord will lead those turning into straits with those working iniquity.'

You will apply to the latter the recompenses, as it is written in Proverbs: 'God sends toward crooked, crooked ways.' Regarding the former recompense, you will punish by sending crooked ways to those who have become crooked through wickedness; but regarding the latter, the recompenses are those being delivered up, which are shown through the sufferings of dishonor and those being reproached. 'Fire and sulfur and a spirit of tempest are the portion of their cup.'

The painful recompenses are often declared in the Scripture by the name of the cup, as in Isaiah: 'Arise, arise, Jerusalem, pouring out the cup of downfall, the bowl of your fury,' and the following; but also in Jeremiah the same is presented from the sound of that voice: 'Take the cup of the wrath of my uncontrolled anger from my hand, and you shall make all the nations drink it, whom I have sent against you.' Does not this also signify the punishment in the things set forth by the portion of the cup divided to them, especially what the fullness of this cup is: 'Fire and sulfur and a spirit of tempest'? The things written in Genesis are not symbols, if they are the punishments having come upon Sodom and Gomorrah from the Lord; toward this fire and sulfur and spirit of tempest is the watering of the cup. The fire declares the [through]...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Deceitful Speech and the Deliverance of the Poor
english: It is a threat of burning, but the divine thing that awakens is rather the fire as a starting point. Along with these, the Spirit indicates a turning of some kind of storm of temptation. And as to what kind of temptation the storm indicates, it is clearly to be learned from that which is written in Isaiah: 'As a storm passing through the desert, coming near, its appearance is fearful and its hardness was announced to me.' Let us therefore flee from impiety, so that this cup may be far from us, and let us live in piety, so that we may drink the intoxicating cup as strongest; for perhaps even that is said: 'The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup.'

For the Lord is just and loved justice, and straightness is his face. For this reason, he watches his eyes over the poor for his salvation, but also upon the sinners he sends snares. For it does not happen by chance, if it becomes of the providence and the judgment of God; for the Lord is just in essence, not merely in participation of justice. Moreover, even if he does not have it by nature, he does not love the justices that are in the many righteous, accepting the intention of each. It is also possible to say another way that he loves justices; since there is justice in the judgment of each, and the judgments of God are many, about which it is written: 'The judgments of the Lord are true and justified'; on the same basis, it is necessary that many justices also exist. And as he is just, so also seeing straightness; and straightness you say is the opinion being regulated toward the right reason; he sees this rejoicing in those who have it. It may also be said regarding straightness in harmony with the second thought concerning the justiceses existing in his unsearchable judgments, which he sees because of the utterly accepting of his face; for God appears present in the works of providence and in the results of the judgments.

As the fullness of the deceit and wickedness of humanity, as if there were no mercy and truth and knowledge of God on the earth, there has become a need for the arrival of the Savior toward us, for the destruction of the existing harm (Ps 11:1). To this end that which is in Jeremiah shall take place: 'Each will play with his neighbor, they will not speak truth; their tongue has learned to speak lies' (Ps 11:2). Why is it not 'the truth' but 'the truths'? The one [reason] is because of the...

The various impieties in transactions, and the wrong opinions in dogmas. For it is not necessary to consider the members of the body being destroyed, but their deceitful use and their boastful speech; for even in Proverbs it is said: 'Remove from yourself a crooked mouth and long deceitful lips from you' (Prov 20:14). Our lips are with us; who is our master? From this audacity the impious man, prospering in finding what he desires, utters a voice like that in Job (Job 10:2): 'Depart from me, I do not wish to know your ways; what is sufficient, what shall we serve him?' For indeed they do not think the prosperity coming to them is due to anything, saying to the Lord: 'Depart; do not make your ways manifest to me; for I do not wish to know them; for what more is of us sufficient, that we may serve you?'

Regarding the impious ones thinking much of themselves as having a boastful tongue and deceitful lips, the poor suffer and the needy groan, not bearing their tyranny (Ps 11:6). Therefore the Lord says: 'I will arise now, having placed my counsel in salvation; I will speak boldly in it against those swelling up proudly of the lowly; and I will release the poor and the needy from suffering and groaning.' You say 'the poor' and in this also 'the needy' to exhort themselves through the weakness coming to them or through the wickedness leading to such a state. Indeed, they have not become superior to suffering and groaning, because the Lord, at the time of the visitation, has arisen and has come to us so that the salvation of those who have suffered and groaned might be made manifest. It is indeed appropriate to hear the following: 'I am a wretched man; who will rescue me from this body of death?' (Rom 7:24). Upon which, speaking boldly thereafter, he says: 'I thank God through Jesus Christ.' For it is shown through these things how Jesus Christ, who rescued the wretched one from the body of death, is the one who said: 'I will arise now,' says the Lord. It is possible to say that the poor are those fallen from wealth, and the needy are those whose living is made through toil; and according to this understanding, the poor and needy are...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Light of Knowledge and the Sleep of Death
english: It is not to be the case that the poor man is not being turned away from necessity. And perhaps what has been said concerning the poor man will be constructed [as an argument], for it is said in the Scripture, 'The rich became poor,' and 'We became very poor'; in agreement with these, what was said concerning the Savior will also be taken: 'As He became rich through our poverty, so that we might become rich through His poverty.'

This also agrees with that concerning the needy: the groaning of the needy, always being in distress and wailing because of the hardship of approaching the destitute. 'I will come' in salvation declares 'I will limit and I will make,' just as He also in the Being placed Himself as heir of all things, the word declaring He limited and manifested Himself as heir. Toward these things, God placed first the apostles and the following in the church, and what was said toward the presbyters of the church: 'The Holy Spirit has placed you to shepherd the church as bishops.' For the word 'placed' shows the demonstration of being limited and made into apostles and bishops.

According to this meaning of preserving, the Savior also said to the Father concerning the disciples: 'Holy Father, keep them; though I am not with them, I kept them, and the evil one did not touch them' (John 17:11). But if this is the meaning because of what was said in Genesis concerning Adam to the serpent: 'He shall guard your head, and you shall guard his heel,' is not 'to guard' (φυλάσαι) and 'to keep' (τηρεῖν) the same thing here? For it appears from it: 'He shall guard your head,' and 'you, his heel.'

The one who is praying sends back the prayer: 'You, Lord, will guard us,' after having done all things from Himself, according to the exhortation saying, 'Keep your heart with all vigilance.' And since these things being made right are not sufficient for the things we strive for against the unforeseen (for if the Lord does not guard a city, in vain the one guarding it stays awake [Ps 127:1]), it is a rule to bring forward a prayer after we have been guarded by ourselves, saying, 'You, Lord, will guard us and will preserve us.' For while He is guarding, let us be courageous, lest we be without counsel for ever; for He is the Most High, O Master, and existing in the high places, according to the approaching height of Your goodness, the [ones]...

You have grown up as a son of men, judging them worthy to have your protection from your providence (Ps 12:4b, 5a). Even if these things are spoken by the Holy [Spirit] in the manner of an embassy, they are not spoken by one subject to the oblivion of God, but by one receiving all things of the petition into himself; and it is clear that the things of his petition are not concerning a sensible light or sleep and death, but concerning the light from the knowledge of God.

For 'enlighten yourselves with the light of knowledge, and draw near to the Lord and be enlightened.' This enlightenment becomes not concerning the sight of the flesh (for this is the sight of the sun) nor any other sensible light of those seeing the sun of righteousness; it is the true light of the eyes of the heart, not of the body, for the noetic powers are the eyes of the inner man. To the one being enlightened, there is blessed life. 'For I am the light of the world,' says the Lord; 'he who walks in me,' he says, 'shall not remain in darkness but shall have the light of life' (John 8:12).

When death comes to the one having been enlightened, it is his sleeping into death, while the one sleeping and dying is the one being in the darkness of ignorance. For he who has given up his eyes to sleep through negligence and laziness will immediately die, falling away from the life which is with virtue; therefore, one must flee from this so-called sleep and death, so that, the eyes of the soul having been enlightened, the enemy may no longer be able to prevail against him, he who formerly thought that we had sinned. (Ps 12:5b, 6)

Since the enemies, those who afflict the righteous, rejoice (Ps 12:6); if it happens that a stumbling occurs because of sin, it is necessary to be grieved for those falling; but even if they rejoice at someone being shaken, I, O Lord, pity my hope in you, and I will not be persuaded to see in myself [the cause]. For I await your salvation coming soon, on which my heart rejoices; for how can he not be glad and rejoice who is experiencing the experience of God's salvation? And if prophecy is being declared concerning the coming of the salvation of God, the Christ, visit. For he, having come for the salvation of the world, brought down those who were leaning upon the shaking ones according to the soul, casting down with them the enemy who was exalting himself.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
